input.rationale: Built and filed the real-cluster witness for the stale-configuration consequence, and corrected the parent account's supplied-fixture premise. The experiment grows a genuine 5-node in-memory cluster: {A,B,C} is bootstrapped from A, entries are committed, A takes a user snapshot recording {A,B,C}, D and E are added through AddVoter with the configuration entry committed at index 8 while A's snapshot stays at index 6, A is shut down, the {A,C} vs {B,D,E} partition is cut, and A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs from its own stores. The harness also records who writes the persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs reads, because a first local variant showed that a node that never ran with the feature enabled stores commit index 0 and therefore does not reproduce the defect: tryStageCommitIndex returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is set. The parent question's interpretation is updated so that the restart-shaped state is no longer described as merely supplied, since this experiment produces it through normal initialization, election, membership change, snapshot and restart, and the election consequence now has its own filed experiment instead of an open limitation.

knowledge.statement: The persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs later reads is written only by tryStageCommitIndex, which returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is true; its callers are dispatchLogs on a leader (staging the commit index as of before the new entries are stored) and the AppendEntries path on a follower (staging min(LeaderCommitIndex, last new entry index)). A node that committed entries while the feature was disabled leaves a stored commit index of 0, so a later restart with the feature enabled replays nothing even though its log is long.
knowledge.conditions: Requires a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the guard is on the running instance's RestoreCommittedLogs value, so mixed deployments (feature off, then on) do not have a persisted commit index to replay.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node keeps the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum. scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, default timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change that is newer than A's last snapshot, then partitioned into {A,C} and {B,D,E}; every node of this deployment runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the commit index that the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, three committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, AddVoter(D) and AddVoter(E), and one further committed apply; no log entry, snapshot or index is written by the harness.

A is shut down (graceful Shutdown) rather than crashed, and its store objects (log store, stable store, snapshot store) are reused for the restart; the in-memory transports are reconnected so that the restarted A can reach only C.
The partition is expressed only by transport disconnection in both directions; the Raft fault model, RPC lifecycles and election timing are untouched.

All five nodes run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled from the start, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; the harness also records that disabling it during the first life leaves the stored commit index at 0.
The cluster is stopped at the end of the test; the observation window uses the nodes' own election timeouts plus a bounded wait for both partitions to elect.
excluded: No process crash or storage fault is injected: A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact.
No on-disk log store is exercised; only the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore.
The conflicting commits are observed at the two leaders; the loss of the minority entry after healing is not executed.
No repository test was executed.

experiment.prefix: The harness creates five InmemTransports with addresses A..E, a full mesh of connections, and per node an InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots). It calls BootstrapCluster(confA, logsA, stableA, snapsA, transA, {A,B,C}), then NewRaft for A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true; it waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if another node won, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A (snapshot index 6, configuration {A,B,C}). It then starts D and E with empty stores and calls AddVoter on the leader for each of them, followed by one more applied command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry (index 8). It emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration A reports and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts the transports so that {A,C} cannot reach {B,D,E}, creates a fresh transport for A connected only to C, and restarts A from its own stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, emitting a 'restart' event with A's state, last applied index and reported configuration. It then waits for a leader in each partition and emits an 'outcome' event with the leaders and terms per partition, the leader count, whether each node in the minority partition is leader, the configurations reported by the restarted A, by C and by the majority leader, the result of an Apply submitted to each leader, the index and term each committed at, the two committed payloads and a derived conflicting_commits operand. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets the in-memory commit index from store.GetCommitIndex() (clamped to the log's last index) and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs enqueues the corresponding commitTuples on fsmMutateCh and then sets lastApplied to that index.
knowledge.conditions: Called during NewRaft, after snapshot restore and before runFSM is started; the log store must implement CommitTrackingLogStore or NewRaft returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore.

knowledge.statement: Outside NewRaft, r.configurations is updated only by the AppendEntries path for entries that are not already present as duplicates with the same term, by processConfigurationLogEntry for those new entries, and by installSnapshot (which sets both latest and committed from the snapshot request); processLogs and the FSM apply path never update the configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Running follower/leader loops on the main thread; duplicate entries (index at or below lastLogIdx with matching term) are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry is reached.

knowledge.statement: A node's election quorum and voter eligibility are computed only from r.configurations.latest (quorumSize counts Voters in latest; the candidate threshold is grantedVotes >= quorumSize, and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's own latest configuration), so a node holding a configuration older than its own committed log counts a smaller voter set and requires fewer votes to become leader.
knowledge.conditions: Election handling on the candidate and voter sides (runCandidate, requestVote); r.configurations.latest is not reconciled with the node's log at any other time.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. Counterevidence and limits: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, and the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log (so a reviewer may argue repair is possible through a later entry or an installed snapshot); the abandoned-write consequence therefore stays a source-reasoned consequence until a multi-node witness exists. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch is queued for index 6/7), so the stale membership is not a missing entry but an unprocessed one.

The minority-quorum election consequence is derived from source (quorumSize/vote admission) and has no executed multi-node witness yet.

knowledge.statement: The persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs later reads is written only by tryStageCommitIndex, which returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is true; its callers are dispatchLogs on a leader (staging the commit index as of before the new entries are stored) and the AppendEntries path on a follower (staging min(LeaderCommitIndex, last new entry index)). interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3.
